contact_id.description: hash key; opaque slug or uuid (e.g. "blue_bottle_wholesale", or a v4 uuid). A SUBJECT: this row IS a party. The id is opaque and gerp-scoped, so a reader groups on it (repeat rate, distinct-customer counts) without publishing it; the name comes only from gerp_profile_id, which a private party does not have

gerp_profile_id.description: the person's or organization's PUBLIC profile (gerp-profiles, one per account, keyed by their account sub). Present = this party is public, so a published row can carry this id and a reader can resolve a display name from it. ABSENT = they are private: the gerp holds their private values and nothing about them is published. This is a REFERENCE, never copied onto a transaction row — someone who publishes a profile later has their whole history resolve retroactively, which stamping at write time could not express

entity_type.description: discriminates which name bucket applies (person vs organization); orthogonal to vendor/customer/employee relationship flags below

email.description: the party's private channel, held by the gerp. A PUBLIC party's contact channel lives on their public profile, which they own; this one is never served

phone.description: e164 preferred; the agent normalizes on write. private channel, same as email

addresses.description: a contact can have multiple addresses; each tagged by address_type (e.g., business + billing + shipping). modules looking for a typed address pick the first matching element, falling back to whichever exists. where a person or firm physically is; never served from the CRM row

unit.description: apartment, suite, unit, floor, room — whichever applies

tax_id.description: EIN for organizations; SSN/ITIN for persons; used for 1099s, W-2s, cross-border billing. a legal identity document

is_vendor.description: true when the firm purchases from this contact; activates the vendor.* bucket

is_customer.description: true when the firm sells to this contact; activates the customer.* bucket

is_employee.description: true when the firm employs this contact; activates the employee.* bucket; persons only

metadata.description: arbitrary key/value for fields not yet promoted into this registry. an unpromoted bag — the registry cannot say what is in it, so it takes the default. Promote a field into the registry with a class to publish it

first_name.description: given name. a private value of a person; the public name lives on their profile

last_name.description: family name; used for alphabetical sort and formal address

name.description: common business name (e.g. "Blue Bottle Coffee"). a FIRM, already a public identity — counterparties publish

legal_name.description: registered legal entity name when different from the common name

terms.description: default payment terms on POs to this vendor

stripe_customer_id.description: for recurring billing; set when the agent or payments module first charges. a handle into the processor's records for this party — resolves to their name, card and address in a system this platform does not govern

stripe_own_customer_id.description: the processor customer this party's OWN saved methods hang off. `stripe_customer_id` is whichever customer the SELECTED method belongs to, which may be someone else's — a gerp billed to a card its account owner saved. Kept apart so choosing that card does not lose track of this party's own.

credit_limit.description: cap on open receivables before the agent declines new invoices

stripe_payment_method_id.description: the card this customer saved for off-session charges (pm_…). written by payments' save_payment_method after they complete a hosted setup page; charged only where a rule instance turns autopay on. a handle into the processor's records — it resolves to a real instrument in a system this platform does not govern

role.description: job title or scope (e.g. "barista", "senior_engineer"). the role, not the worker — a role publishes

hourly_rate.description: snapshot at hire; shift rows in the labor module carry the rate at shift time. cost structure, which is the product. It publishes on a row whose subject is absent unless that person is public

payroll_processor_id.description: the ID this employee has in the owner's payroll processor (ADP, Gusto, Stripe). a handle into the payroll processor's record of this person
